newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma aide slams IMF over delayed Ukraine credit.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma aide slams IMF over delayed Ukraine credit.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma's chief of staff on Thursday accused the International Monetary Fund (IMF) of helping conservatives in parliament by delaying a multi-billion credit to the former Soviet republic.

Delivery of the $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility, to succeed last year's $867 million stand-by agreement, has been held up by delays in meeting a list of 41 IMF conditions -- particularly the months-late 1997 budget.
"We think the IMF must take the political situation in modern Ukraine into account," Yevhen Kushnaryov, head of Kuchma's administration, told a news conference.

"Non-delivery of the aid works in favour of leftist forces because it makes the political and social situation worse," he added, referring to conservatives in parliament who have blocked reforms proposed by the government and backed by the IMF.
"The IMF is failing to see the difficulties of legally implementing economic reforms through parliament," he added.

A huge backlog of wages owed to coal miners and government employees and a poor standard of living have left many Ukrainians disillusioned about independence won from Moscow six years ago, with some longing for a return to Soviet times.
Parliament, where communists dominate, and the government have blamed each other for delays in the budget which was expected to be given a third and final reading late on Thursday.
Ukraine has fulfilled about 30 of the 41 IMF conditions, but the budget is seen as crucial, and parliament is due to shut down until September in mid-July.
Kuchma met the IMF's deputy managing director last week and his aides expressed optimism over the credit, which Ukraine says could win final agreement from the Fund next month.
